newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - No need to panic, says Dykes.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - No need to panic, says Dykes.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, Feb 20 - New Zealand's cricket selectors aren't about to panic as they seek answers to the 2-0 test series loss to England, NZPA reports.
New Zealand went into the third test at Lancaster Park last Friday needing a win to square the rubber after losing the second test by an innings and 68 runs.

Unlike that loss in Wellington, New Zealand were competitive for much of the third test before losing by four wickets on Tuesday as England scored more than 300 to win a test for only the second time in their history.
Now New Zealand have five one-day internationals against England before playing two tests against Sri Lanka at Dunedin and Hamilton next month.

The England test series threw up one shining light for the New Zealanders in teenage left-arm spinner Daniel Vettori while there were encouraging returns to the national side for fast-medium pair Heath Davis and Geoff Allott.
Vettori took seven wickets in three innings over the last two tests and showed he has special gifts.
Allott and Davis were lively and were capable of troubling the English batsmen and, at 25, they have their best years ahead of them.
Opening batsman Blair Pocock, out of action since the 1994 tour of England because of a long-term shoulder injury, made a satisfying return to test cricket.
There were two half-centuries in his six innings -- 70 in the first innings of the drawn opening test in Auckland and 64 in the second innings at Wellington -- and an average of 30.
That gave an indication that Pocock and Northern Districts team mate Bryan Young could develop a long-term opening partnership.
Those positives were outweighed by the two losses in the series, but chairman of selectors Ross Dykes intends keeping faith with the current squad.
"We have made significant changes and we'd like to think we've been moderately successful," Dykes said.
"In the case of Vettori, he's been highly successful; in the case of Allott and Davis, they've been successful.
"We're not in the habit of trying to make wholesale changes. What we're trying to do now is establish players we think fit the pattern and perform well."
New Zealand's problem in the test series was the inconsistency of the batting.
At times, Stephen Fleming, Nathan Astle, Pocock, Young and Chris Cairns all played impressive, skilful innings.

However, in each test the batting let the side down -- before lunch on the final day at Auckland; in the two hours' play on the first day at Wellington, and again on the fourth afternoon when three wickets fell at 125; and in the second
innings at Lancaster Park.
Dykes is hoping the batsmen absorb the lessons from the test series.
"They did create an opportunity to win a test (in Christchurch). We've got limited players to pick from but we believe we're playing our best players.
"At the end of the day these batsmen are going to learn a lot -- one would hope they learn a lot."
